question:
I am handing over a finished system to a client whose in-house team will keep developing it after delivery. Besides the program itself, what written material should I prepare for the client, for its end users and for my own organization, and for how long should it be retained?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).

### A — Documentation for the client's in-house team (technical / developer-facing)

**Guideline 7 — Supply users with the information they need to operate the system safely and correctly.**

### C — Documentation for your own organisation (internal records)

**Guideline 9 — Document relevant facts, significant risks and trade-offs, and any warnings about dangerous consequences.**
Internal documentation for your own organisation must record relevant facts, significant risks and trade-offs made during development, and warnings of undesirable or dangerous consequences from use or misuse of the software. It must also record relevant information about attributes, licence types, and sourcing of third-party components.

(source: "[SWEBOK excerpt bcc817576a2ea720bc51] attribute, license type, and sourcing." — `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Professional Practice and Collaboration in Software Engineering/Professional Responsibility and Intellectual Property in Software Engineering/Documentation and Requirements Trade-off Management/Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md`)

**Guideline 10 — Conduct a formal project-closure review and archive all project materials.**
When the project reaches closure, evaluate success criteria, document the degree of requirements satisfaction and any known problems, and document relevant stakeholders' acceptance. After closure, archive all project materials in accordance with stakeholder-agreed rules covering archival methods, location, duration, and destruction of sensitive information.

### D — Retention period

**Guideline 11 — Keep all documents for at least the full product life cycle, or longer if regulations require.**
[SWEBOK excerpt cf20421fe740a3ccd198] organisational or regulatory requirements, whichever is longer.

(source: "[SWEBOK excerpt 3195bf83cb2eca8378f7]." — `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Professional Practice and Collaboration in Software Engineering/Professional Responsibility and Intellectual Property in Software Engineering/Documentation and Requirements Trade-off Management/Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md`)

### Summary table

| Audience | Key documents |
|---|---|
| **Client's developers** | Functional specifications · Software design docs · Test suite · Operating-environment description · SRS · Tool and method descriptions · Problem log · VDD · Release notes · Installation instructions · Maintenance plan · All SCIs |
| **End users / operators / admins** | User manuals covering safe/unsafe use · Sensitive-data protection guidance · Warnings and critical procedures · Installation and upgrade instructions |
| **Your own organisation** | Risk and trade-off records · Licence/sourcing records · Closure report (acceptance, known problems) · Archived project materials |
| **Retention** | Minimum: entire product life cycle, extended by any applicable organisational or regulatory obligation |
